chore(openai): align model catalog capabilities with live API audit (#25462)

## Background

We ran a live audit of the OpenAI model catalog: every declared
capability cell was checked against OpenAI's docs and probed against the
API through the SDK. A handful of cells contradicted what the API
actually does, and a few listed model IDs now come back as
model-not-found. The API result is the source of truth here, so this PR
fixes the catalog values that were wrong. The catalog shape stays the
same.

The audit files are here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/25485

## Summary

Catalog values corrected to match the live API:

- `flexProcessing` → `false`: `gpt-6.2-astra` and `gpt-6.2-sol`. The API
rejects `service_tier=flex` for these models.
- `chatFunctionToolsWithReasoning` → `false`: all GPT-6 models plus
`gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini`, and `gpt-5.4-nano`. Chat
Completions returns "Function tools with reasoning_effort are not
supported".
- `configurationUpdates` → `true`: `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-5.6-luna`,
`gpt-5.6-sol`, and `gpt-5.6-terra`. The API accepts request-level
configuration updates.
- `priorityProcessing` → `true`: `gpt-5-nano` and `gpt-5.4-nano`. The
API accepts the priority tier.
- Transcription `streaming` → `true`: `whisper-1`, `gpt-4o-transcribe`,
and `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`. Realtime transcription accepts them.

New list `openaiDiscontinuedModelIds` for model IDs that the API now
answers with model-not-found: `gpt-5-chat-latest`,
`gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.2-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.3-chat-latest`,
`gpt-5-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`, `gpt-image-1`,
`dall-e-2`, and `dall-e-3`. Their entries stay in the catalog so
existing model IDs still type-check.

Tests now use the corrected values. Where a test covers a warn-and-omit
path, it uses a model that still lacks that capability. The generated
OpenAI and Azure capability tables were regenerated with `pnpm
generate:model-capabilities-docs`, which
`verify:model-capabilities-docs` requires. No hand-written docs changed.

Audit results this PR leaves alone:
- `MISSING` rows are docs fields the catalog has no column for.
- `UNVERIFIED` rows didn't produce enough evidence.
- Chat rejects `reasoningEffort: 'max'`, but the chat model already
filters `max` out.
- GPT-6 `promptCacheRetention` and `tts-1`/`tts-1-hd` `instructions`:
the API accepts both, but OpenAI documents them as replaced or ignored,
so they stay unsupported.
- The `responsesLogprobsRequireNonReasoning` rows for GPT-4.x come from
a probe that sent a reasoning effort to non-reasoning models.

merged)

- [ ] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)

commit.message:
fix(harness-claude-code): drop a subagent's host tool call record once its result passes (#25310)

## Background

As #25309 describes, a host tool call that the main agent made after a
subagent made the same call, with the same input, never reached the
host.
- A subagent's messages carry `parent_tool_use_id` and are forwarded
raw, so the bridge never sees the subagent's `tool_result`.
- So the `mcpHandlerCalls` record that the subagent's handler call left
stayed for the rest of the turn.
- The main agent's identical `tool_use` then matched that record in
`findMcpHandlerCallId`. The stream path treated the call as already
sent, and the handler found it already in `emittedToolCallIds`.
- Neither path emitted a `tool-call`, so `turn.requestToolResult` never
resolved and the turn waited.

## Summary

In `createEmitStreamEvent`, the branch that forwards a subagent's
messages now drops the `mcpHandlerCalls` record named by each
`tool_result` in a subagent's `user` message.
- That record belongs to the subagent's own call, which has been
answered by then.
- In production on Claude Code 2.1.319, the bridge received the results
of both a foreground and a background subagent's host calls: 12 of 12 in
a turn of each kind. So dropping the record covers both.
- Records of the main agent's calls are untouched, so their
name-and-input matching works as before. That includes a handler call
that runs first under an id the reported `tool_use` doesn't carry.

Tagging every handler record with its `claudecode/toolUseId` would also
stop the stale match. But a handler call that ran first under an id its
`tool_use` doesn't carry would then no longer be matched, and the host
would run that call twice. The second new test pins this. The existing
"deduplicates host tool results when handler metadata cannot be matched"
test stores its record directly, without an id, so it passes under
either design.

Tests, in `src/bridge/index.test.ts`:
- **sends a host tool call the main agent repeats after a subagent made
the same call.** It plays the order that Claude Code produces: the
subagent's call, its result, then the main agent's identical call. The
host gets both calls and both are answered. On `main` it fails: the main
agent's call never reaches the host.
- **runs a host tool call once when its handler runs first under another
id.** It fails if the records are tagged with `claudecode/toolUseId`
instead.

All 12 bridge test files pass (`vitest --config vitest.node.config.js
--run src/bridge`, 317 tests). `tsc --noEmit`, `oxfmt --check` and
`oxlint` pass on the changed files.

## End-to-End Verification

Not run end-to-end. The failure needs a live Claude Code turn in which a
subagent calls a host tool and the main agent then makes the identical
call.
- With this repository's harness, that means a Vercel Sandbox and a live
model.
- A model doesn't produce that sequence on demand, and I didn't have a
reproduction that runs it deterministically.

We observed the defect in production with `@ai-sdk/harness-claude-code`
1.0.188, `@ai-sdk/harness` 1.0.184, Claude Code 2.1.319 (agent SDK
0.3.319) and a Vercel Sandbox:
- The session transcript ended at the main agent's `tool_use` for the
host tool, with no result.
- The host recorded no execution of that call.
- The Claude Code process stayed idle, with no model connection open,
until the sandbox stopped.
- The subagent had made the same call with the same input minutes
earlier, and the host had answered it.

The same change, applied as a patch to the published 1.0.188 bridge,
passes an equivalent replay through that installed bridge. The replay
fails without the change.

## Checklist

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Future Work

Three cases still leave a subagent's record in place:
- A subagent's host call that reaches the handler without
`claudecode/toolUseId` is keyed by a random id, so its `tool_result`
can't name it. Claude Code passed the id on every call we saw.
- A main-agent call made while the subagent's identical call is still in
flight can still match the record.
- A call from a subagent that another subagent started, if its messages
don't reach the bridge.

Closes #25446

fix(harness): keep sandbox channel connected while a large frame is still transferring (#25420)

## Background

the sandbox channel heartbeat terminates a socket after two unanswered
pings. On a slow link, pongs queue behind a large bridge event still in
transit, so the heartbeat killed a progressing connection; the reconnect
resumed from the same cursor, the bridge replayed the same frame, and
the loop repeated.

the heartbeat now counts inbound bytes on the underlying socket as a
sign of life. A fully silent peer is still terminated after two
unanswered pings

fix(assemblyai): decode base64 audio before uploading it for transcription (#25424)

## Background

`TranscriptionModelV4` call options allow `audio` to be a `Uint8Array`
or a base64-encoded `string`. The AssemblyAI transcription model passed
`options.audio` straight to AssemblyAI's `POST /v2/upload` endpoint,
which expects the raw file. Given a base64 string, it uploaded the
base64 text itself, and AssemblyAI failed the transcript:

```
Transcription failed: Transcoding failed. File type text/plain (ASCII text, with very long lines (53560), with no line terminators) may be unsupported or an unexpected error occurred.
```

`transcribe()` converts audio to a `Uint8Array` before calling the
model, so it was not affected. The failure appears when the model's
`doGenerate` is called with a base64 string.

## Summary

- Decode a base64 `audio` string with `convertBase64ToUint8Array` before
uploading, as the other transcription models that upload a file do (for
example Fish Audio, Groq, Mistral and Rev.ai).
- Add a test that calls `doGenerate` with a base64 string and asserts
the upload body is the decoded bytes.

## End-to-End Verification

Exercised the public provider API
(`createAssemblyAI().transcription('assemblyai-stt-3-7').doGenerate(...)`)
against the live AssemblyAI API, with the package built from this
checkout for both runs. The "before" run is this branch with the change
to `assemblyai-transcription-model.ts` stashed and the package rebuilt.

Reproduction, saved outside the checkout as
`/tmp/assemblyai-base64-repro.mjs`:

```js
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createAssemblyAI } from '@ai-sdk/assemblyai';

console.log('package:', import.meta.resolve('@ai-sdk/assemblyai'));

const model = createAssemblyAI().transcription('assemblyai-stt-3-7');
const bytes = new Uint8Array(readFileSync(process.argv[2]));

for (const [label, audio] of [
  ['Uint8Array', bytes],
  ['base64 string', Buffer.from(bytes).toString('base64')],
]) {
  try {
    const { text, durationInSeconds } = await model.doGenerate({
      audio,
      mediaType: 'audio/mpeg',
    });
    console.log(`${label}: ok`, { text, durationInSeconds });
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(`${label}: failed -`, error.message);
  }
}
```

Setup and run (requires `ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY`). The script is piped on
stdin from `examples/ai-functions` so `@ai-sdk/assemblyai` resolves to
the workspace package:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/assemblyai...
cd examples/ai-functions
node --input-type=module - ../../packages/assemblyai/src/transcript-test.mp3 < /tmp/assemblyai-base64-repro.mjs
```

Before:

```
package: file://<checkout>/packages/assemblyai/dist/index.js
Uint8Array: ok { text: 'Hello from the Vercel AI SDK.', durationInSeconds: 3 }
base64 string: failed - Transcription failed: Transcoding failed. File type text/plain (ASCII text, with very long lines (53560), with no line terminators) may be unsupported or an unexpected error occurred. See supported formats at https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/faq/what-audio-and-video-file-types-are-supported-by-your-api. [...]
```

After:

```
package: file://<checkout>/packages/assemblyai/dist/index.js
Uint8Array: ok { text: 'Hello from the Vercel AI SDK.', durationInSeconds: 3 }
base64 string: ok { text: 'Hello from the Vercel AI SDK.', durationInSeconds: 3 }
```
